blocks.prompt: 9 By computing the area of triangle \(ABC\) check whether the points are collinear where \(A(0, 4)\), \(B(3, 2)\) and \(C(6, 0)\).
blocks.explanation:
Collinearity test by area (Corollary of 5.7): the points are collinear exactly when \(\Delta = 0\).
Compute \(\Delta\) with the area formula and look at the result.
steps:
Given: \(A(0, 4)\), \(B(3, 2)\), \(C(6, 0)\).
To find: whether \(A\), \(B\), \(C\) are collinear.
Method: \(\Delta = \frac{1}{2}[x_1(y_2 - y_3) + x_2(y_3 - y_1) + x_3(y_1 - y_2)]\); \(\Delta = 0\) means collinear.

Conclusion
\(\Delta = 0\), so the points are collinear.
Why: three points enclose zero area only if they lie on one line.

Check:
\[m_{AB} = \dfrac{2 - 4}{3 - 0} = -\dfrac{2}{3}\]
\[m_{BC} = \dfrac{0 - 2}{6 - 3} = -\dfrac{2}{3}\]
Equal slopes through the common point \(B\) \(\checkmark\)
